precepts.text: Which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God. That line, Seth's line, were the sons of God. Abel was one, but Cain killed him; then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel.
precepts.point: The earth also was corrupt before God: because the sons of God started to mingle with the daughters of men, Cain's children. Cain gained dominion on the earth. And the earth was filled with violence: just like Cain was violent. Is the earth full of violence today? Yes. The end of all flesh is come before me; behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Luke traces Christ's line all the way back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” There it is written plainly. Adam was the son of God, and that line, Seth's line, were the sons of God of Genesis 6.

Abel was one of them, but Cain killed him. Then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel, and the line of the sons of God continued through him.

So “the sons of God saw the daughters of men” is Seth's line looking upon Cain's daughters. What followed is why “it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth.” The sons of God started to behave like Cain and his daughters, and God said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth”: destroy everything and start over. “The earth also was corrupt before God,” because the sons of God mingled with Cain's children; Cain gained dominion, “and the earth was filled with violence,” just as Cain was violent.

precepts.text: Says the same thing. You want the baptism of the spirit, because the fire is coming to clean up everything else. Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor; the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable. That is talking about judgment.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
Luke says the same thing, just in case anybody relapsed and wants to jump in the pickle juice: “I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire”. This is not talking about water.

“Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.” That is talking about judgment.

So you want the baptism of the Spirit, because the fire is coming to clean up everything else, and that is what Christ is coming with. The one Spirit that baptizes us into one body is the cleansing that gathers the wheat into his garner; the chaff that refuses it will be burned with fire unquenchable.

precepts.text: Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God. That is the lineage of the sons of God: the chosen line comes through Seth, who replaced Abel. Write that down so the question never confuses you again.
precepts.point: Why did God allow it? Because the sons of God broke God's law before it.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Genesis 6 says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men,” and the question always comes: who are the sons of God, and what line do they come out of? Luke 3:38 answers it at the end of Christ’s genealogy: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.”

That is the lineage of the sons of God. Adam is called the son of God, and the chosen line runs from him through Seth. Of Adam’s sons, Abel was put to death, and Seth replaced him; the sons of God came out of Seth’s line, down to Enos and on to Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

Write that down so the next time the question comes up you are not confused. It explains the promise to Abram: “thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs.” The sons of God of Seth’s line broke God’s law by mixing with the daughters of men, and the judgment came down on the same chosen line: Jacob’s children went into Egypt and served in hard bondage four hundred years.

precepts.text: John came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins: the same river Naaman was cleansed in.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
We read about Naaman going down into the river Jordan to be cleansed. Luke brings us back to that same river: John “came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins; As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”

The baptism of repentance, for the remission of sins, preached about Jordan. Naaman was washed of his leprosy in the Jordan, and John preached the washing away of sins in the same Jordan. Nothing is accidental with the Most High.

It was Christ who healed Naaman, working through Elisha by his spirit. And John in the Jordan was preparing the way of that same Lord.

precepts.text: Jesus began to be about thirty years of age, being as was supposed the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli, of Matthat, of Levi, of Melchi. As was supposed refers to Joseph. Heli's line has no Eleazar or Matthan, so it is a different bloodline: Luke follows Mary from her cousin Elisabeth onward and names her husband in her place, which is why no woman is named in Luke 3 while women are named in Matthew 1. Not knowing something does not make you an idiot; pick up the phone and ask a bishop or deacon. Making it up does.
precepts.point: Boaz begat Obed of Ruth is where levirate marriage actually shows up, but we will not be bamboozled by a spin move into an Old Testament law that has nothing to do with the question asked.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
Matthew 1 is “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham”: the link between Christ and the royal seat promised through David's loins, through Solomon and their sons. At the end of it: “Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob; And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary”. Someone claimed Jacob and Heli were brothers. You do not read that anywhere in the Bible.

Luke 3: “And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”. Did it say the son of Heli? No. “As was supposed” refers to him being the son of Joseph. It had nothing to do with Heli at all.

Now line them up. Luke goes on: “Which was the son of Matthat, which was the son of Levi, which was the son of Melchi”. Even if Matthat and Matthan were the same man spelled differently, Matthan's father in Matthew is Eleazar, and in Luke Matthat's father is Levi. Eliud and Eleazar are not mentioned in Luke 3 at all. These are two completely different bloodlines. They do not expect you to bounce back and forth and make sure it lines up; they bank on you not fact-checking.

Matthew starts with Joseph: the angel comes to Joseph, you follow his story, and his lineage is given. Luke chose to follow Mary: it begins with her cousin Elisabeth and the babe leaping in her womb, and in the third chapter it gives her lineage, all men. That is why not one woman is named in Luke 3, while some women are named in Matthew 1. Where it would have said Mary, it names her husband.

And “Booz begat Obed of Ruth” is where the levirate marriage actually shows up, but we will not be bamboozled by a spin move into an Old Testament law that has nothing to do with the question. Not knowing something does not make you an idiot. Pick up the phone and ask a Bishop or a Deacon. Making it up does.

precepts.text: Christ's lineage on his mother's side runs back through Seth to Adam, the son of God.
precepts.point: When Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam.

note.label: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam

precepts.why:
Christ’s lineage on his mother’s side runs straight back through this book of the generations of Adam: “Which was the son of Cainan, which was the son of Arphaxad, which was the son of Sem, which was the son of Noe, which was the son of Lamech, Which was the son of Mathusala, which was the son of Enoch, which was the son of Jared, which was the son of Maleleel, which was the son of Cainan, Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.”

Adam was the son of God, and chapter 5 is his direct lineage. That lineage is the sons of God of chapter 6, and through Shem it ties the Israelites directly to the line of Adam. That is why, when Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam, the son of God.

precepts.text: Annas and Caiaphas being the high priests, showing Annas kept the title as the former high priest alongside the ruling Caiaphas.
precepts.point: Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in Isaiah 53 and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“Annas and Caiaphas being the high priests, the word of God came unto John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness.” Two high priests named at once.

Annas had been high priest around 6 to 15 AD and kept the title even after the Romans ejected him, while Caiaphas, his son-in-law, was the official high priest the year Christ was killed. That is why Luke names them together, and why both sat in the council that gathered against Peter and John.

points: Luke 2:1 names Caesar Augustus; Luke 3:1 names Tiberius. These are the feathers we are reading about in Esdras. When you read the four gospels, Tiberius is the Caesar of the time Christ was an adult.

The fourth feather: Caligula, born AD 12, died AD 41, reign AD 37 to 41, the first Roman emperor to be assassinated; initiated construction of Roman aqueducts. Within the book of Acts his reign roughly corresponds to Acts 7 (the death of Stephen) through early Acts 12: the persecution following Stephen's death and Saul's conversion (circa AD 35 to 36), Peter's vision and ministry in Acts 10 and 11 around the time Caligula's persecution of Jews in Alexandria prompted a crisis, and Acts 12 (the death of James and the imprisonment of Peter under Herod Agrippa I) just after Caligula's assassination.
